body:
Measured, same green commit `3a240b7fb`, all tests:

| Run | Machine | Cache | Wall time | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Post-merge gate (batch tier, steps one at a time) | self-hosted runner | warm | **53.4 min** (898 steps; sum of step times 44.9 min) | green |
| `cargo nextest run` (same scope as batch: workspace minus kernel, minus SLOW_BINARIES, no ignored) + batch clippy | Hetzner ccx43, 16 vCPU | **cold, sccache off** | **18.8 min** (build + tests 17.4 min, of which tests 12.3 min; clippy 1.4 min) | **8465 tests run: 8465 passed**, 77 skipped |

Average CPU during the nextest run: 80 % (load 27 on 16 vCPU). The batch gate's own log shows why it is slow: 731 of 898 steps take <= 1 s, and the floor is the build (237 s) plus the longest step (motion lib, 287 s), about 9 min with full parallelism.

So nextest (or lanes in `xtask`) is about 3x faster from a cold start; with a warm cache it should come in well under the 53 min. Scripts: `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude camcraft-kernel --no-fail-fast -E 'not (binary(finish3d) & package(camcraft-motion)) and not (binary(pivot5d) & package(camcraft-motion)) and not (binary(flow) & package(camcraft-motion)) and not (binary(center_cut_multiaxis) & package(camcraft-app))'`. Not yet checked: doc-tests (nextest skips them), and whether the gate's known-fail/VOID bookkeeping maps onto nextest's output.
